text:
alex: heads up — saw 3 OOMs on prod-rt-03 during the 00:30 ingest spike. stack points to allocator failing to satisfy workspace for kernel-selection path 2. can we quick sync on mitigations?

sara: saw the alerts too. are they all kv-heavy requests or a mix? :thinking_face:

alex: mostly kv + long-prefix chat logs. pattern: big prefix -> kernel picks big workspace -> no slab available -> OOM. logs attached below.

alex: log excerpt: `RuntimeError: cudamalloc failed after 1.2s (requested 210MB) -- workspace_alloc failed`

jia: thanks. first pass: we should trim cold KV buckets proactively during high-pressure windows, and reduce per-request workspace targets for kernel path 2. don't want full-scale evictions yet.

matt: agree. propose emergency buffer realignment: 1) enable allocator.run_time_trim=true, 2) lower workspace_target_mb for kernel selector from 256 -> 96 for ephemeral requests, 3) add request-shaping rule to cap concurrent long-prefix jobs per instance.

riya: adding a short config proposal below for ops to stage quickly: 
```
runtime:
  allocator:
    runtime_trim: true
    slab_target_mb: 48
    aggressive_release: on
  kernel_selector:
    path2_workspace_mb: 96
  kvcache:
    ttl_seconds: 90
    eviction_policy: lru_weighted
routing:
  request_shaping:
    max_concurrent_long_prefix: 12
    slowpath_margin_ms: 80
  fallback:
    on_oom_model: small-rt-1-cpu
```

sara: that looks good. two comments: (1) lowering path2 workspace may increase latency for those requests — we should set a canary with 10% traffic first. (2) kvcache ttl 90s might thrash; prefer 120s with weighted eviction.

alex: noted. plan: canary 10% on prod-rt-03, apply allocator runtime_trim and path2_workspace=96, kvcache ttl=120, max_concurrent_long_prefix=12. if OOMs persist, flip on fallback to small-rt-1-cpu for miss and add circuit-breaker.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by alex: deploy/redwood/runtime-config#hotfix/allocator-trim -> staging -> prod-rt-03 canary(10%)

perf-bot: quick profiling snapshot (prod-rt-03 pre-change):
  - median GPU mem used per worker: 8.7GB
  - 95p GPU mem used: 11.9GB
  - top 10 offending requests: long-prefix+kv (avg workspace req 210MB)
  - KV coldset retention: 240s

perf-bot: predicted impact after patch: -20% peak memory, +3-10% latency on shaped requests, reduced OOM probability by ~80% for observed spike distribution (model: sampled traces).

jia: small technical note — allocator.runtime_trim uses cudaFree to return whole slabs; we saw fragmentation improvements in last sim run. but it can trigger brief latency spikes due to OS/GPU driver activity. that's why canary and rate-limit is important.

riya: alternative safer option: enable slab soft-reserve for critical low-latency kernels and do aggressive trimming only on non-critical kernels. that keeps p95 tight for interactive flows.

matt: good call. propose we mark 'interactive' routing tags with slab_reserve_mb: 256 and reduce for batch/long-prefix to 96. that preserves latency SLAs.

alex: agreed. updated action list: 
  - A: push hotfix canary (alex) -> allocator.runtime_trim=true, path2_workspace=96, kvcache.ttl=120, max_concurrent_long_prefix=12, fallback disabled initially
  - B: monitor p50/p95/p99 and OOMs for 30m (sara + perf-bot)
  - C: if OOM rate > 1 per 30m, enable fallback to small-rt-1-cpu and set circuit-breaker for that route (jia)
  - D: post-mortem doc capturing root cause and perf regs (matt)

sara: starting canary rollout now. tagging @oncall for visibility. :rocket:

perf-bot: canary started on prod-rt-03 subset (10%). initial memory curves look promising — peak worker mem down ~18% in first 5m.

alex: nice. keep an eye on latency tail. also check kernel-selection logs to confirm path2 still used but with smaller workspace.

perf-bot: kernel-selection summary (canary 5m window): path2 chosen 42% -> avg workspace request 98MB, fallback to path1 increased slightly.

riya: observing a handful of requests moving to fallback CPU model; that's expected under tight headroom. confirm SLA impact minimal?

perf-bot: CPU fallback latency p95 is 320ms higher vs GPU for those requests, but overall user-facing p95 across traffic slice increased by ~6ms.

alex: given tradeoffs, keep this config for next 24h and schedule a deeper perf/regression run. I'll start the post-incident checklist. thanks team. :thumbsup:

matt: for postmortem let's capture: kernel selector heuristics, workspace sizing defaults, kvcache TTL interplay, allocator fragmentation metrics, and a runbook for turning on slab_reserve for interactive routes.

jia: also add a note about driver-level cudaFree noise and how to detect (spike in GPU sync time).

sara: oncall acknowledged, monitoring continues. ping if anything spikes.

alex: closing thread after 24h stable window or if we flip fallback.

deploy-bot: canary promoted to 70% at 1749999188 by sara (health checks green).

perf-bot: final canary report (60m): OOMs reduced to zero on canary slice, p95 overall +4ms, 95p mem down 19%. recommended to roll to 100% and document change.

riya: rolling to 100% now.

alex: thanks everyone. will draft the postmortem and one-off mitigation script.

matt: saving config snippets into infra/ops/quickfixs and will attach to PM.

alex: :white_check_mark:
